questions.q: How does INAV differ from Betaflight?
options: It runs only on H7 boards
It adds navigation and fixed wings
questions.explain: INAV is manual flight plus navigation on the same boards.

options: With the sticks, as in old versions
questions.explain: Stick arming was removed in INAV 2.2.

questions.q: Why may INAV refuse to arm?
options: High P and low motor KV
No fix or no compass for navigation
questions.explain: A protection: navigation modes without a fix are dangerous.

options: The takeoff point at the first arm
questions.explain: A predefined safe point that replaces home for RTH: up to 8 points, the nearest one within safehome_max_distance.

options: The vehicle type and the mixer

questions.q: Which sensors does a multirotor need for RTH?
options: GPS and an optical flow camera
GPS, a compass and a barometer
questions.explain: Heading — the compass, altitude — the baro, position — GPS. That is what docs/Failsafe.md 9.1 says; without a compass (since 7.1) the heading comes from GPS while moving, and in 9.1 it can be set on the ground with a stick command.

questions.q: What does INAV use to estimate position?
options: A Kalman filter modeled on PX4's EKF2
questions.explain: That is why GPS quality matters more than in ArduPilot.

questions.q: How does INAV differ from ArduPilot in purpose?
options: Navigation on a simple base that is familiar after Betaflight, without a companion computer or Lua
INAV has more modes and an EKF
questions.explain: INAV is manual flight plus navigation; ArduPilot is a full autopilot with an EKF, Lua and companion computers.
